Purpose and exclusions

Make accepted actions readable without allowing particles, sprite frames or sounds to grant damage, resources or loot. A missed cue may look wrong but must never leave gameplay stuck.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Create DA_CueSet_Common with mappings for Cleave, ArrowImpact, OreHit, WoodHit, FishBite, CraftComplete and LevelUp; rights-cleared sound/VFX assignments remain explicit authoring tasks.
  2. Create Niagara systems only after checking the installed Niagara tooling; use engine primitive debug circles and text markers until assets exist. Do not treat a particle collision event as a server hit.
  3. Attach URPGPresentationCueComponent to the player/enemy presentation root; define foot and hand offsets in DA_AnimationSet_Common per facing/page.
  4. Bind audio sliders in WBP_Options to local audio settings, not replicated attributes. Include mute, subtitle/visual cue toggles and reduced-flash controls.
  5. Place CueEmitter_A in L_ArtLab and trigger each cue from the diagnostics adapter with no gameplay state changes; repeat during a two-client combat run.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Functions, commands and event bindings

Project custom contracts are not engine/plugin nodes. A read-only asset participates through its consumer; it does not inherit that consumer’s mutation methods. Backend endpoint pages label transport proposals explicitly.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Construct with only safe defaults; no service calls or world scans from construction scripts.
  2. Inject current owner/definition/session and subscribe once after readiness. Possession and replicated state may arrive in either order; guard initialization.
  3. Accept only permitted commands under current identity/epoch; keep local UI/cosmetic prediction separate from committed state.
  4. After server/backend result apply only matching request generation and nonstale revision; late reply to old body does not mutate new body.
  5. On death, transfer, disconnect, restart or teardown cancel transient work, clear input/timers, unbind delegates and release weak observers. Durable receipts remain authoritative.
  6. On reconnect create fresh runtime objects from current committed snapshot; never deserialize old Actor/widget pointers or rerun initial grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in Audio, particles and 2D/3D presentation cues. Rule owner: URPGPresentationCueComponent. This asset’s role is Make accepted actions readable without allowing particles, sprite frames or sounds to grant damage, resources or loot. A missed cue may look wrong but must never leave gameplay stuck.

  1. Input may start an inexpensive predicted swing cue with its local action correlation.
  2. Server accepts or rejects the action using combat/gathering rules independently of the cue.
  3. Accepted presentation state includes action identity, target/world point and start time; remote clients resolve the authored cue.
  4. The cue adapter samples the current facing anchor, spawns world-space projectile/impact particles or plays sound, and avoids triggering twice when prediction is confirmed.
  5. Rejected action fades/cancels the predicted cue; late remote presentation catches up within a bounded visual window.
  6. Destroy or pool visual components on completion, possession change and zone unload; no cue callback calls a reward or health setter.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_ArtLab / CueEmitter_A / two remote clients. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Missing cue asset -> one rate-limited MissingCue warning; gameplay still completes.
Late confirm for canceled action -> no second sound/particle and no gameplay grant.
Zone unload while particle alive -> destroy/pool safely, no stale Actor dereference.
Muted audio -> fishing bite still has a readable visual timer.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not duplicate a native rule in Blueprint, assume a planned type is compiled, or keep callbacks/owners valid after world or session replacement.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
